input.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE

contradicting_evidence.quote: The incremental tariffs announced in 2025 and expected to be in place on August 7 will be a headwind to profitability during the remainder of the year.
We expect about 55 percent of the net incremental tariff impact will be incurred in Construction Industries.
We anticipate around 50 percent of the incremental tariff costs will be in Construction Industries, 20 percent in Resource Industries and 30 percent in Power & Energy.

input.reasoning_summary:
The claim that "Caterpillar handled the 2025 tariff environment well" is a qualitative/interpretive assertion about the company's performance in managing tariff challenges during 2025. 

The evidence shows that:
1. Incremental tariffs announced in 2025 were described as "a headwind to profitability during the remainder of the year" (E2)
2. The company took "initial mitigating actions to reduce the impact" but noted that "tariff and trade negotiations continue to be fluid" (E2)
3. The company was "considering all options to further reduce the impact from incremental tariffs going forward" (E2)
4. Significant incremental tariff costs were expected across all segments (E1, E3)

While the evidence shows Caterpillar acknowledged the tariff challenges and took some mitigating actions, there is no evidence that affirmatively establishes they "handled" the situation "well." The filings describe tariffs as a headwind and discuss ongoing efforts to mitigate impacts, but do not provide outcome data or assessments that would support a conclusion that the company performed well in managing these challenges. The evidence suggests challenges and mitigation efforts but does not establish successful handling of the tariff environment.
